catalog_quote: L'accent tonique existe en langue Banda; nous avons pu en déterminer les règles suivantes qu semblent être très générales: Rèc.le I. — Dans les mots de deux ou trois syllabes, l'accent tonique se place sur la première. Ex. : mots de deux syllabes : yavrou, chien; ... kâga, montagne. ... Mois de trois syllabes : kôkora, flèche; sUima, être. Règle II. — Dans les mots de quatre syllabes, Taccent tonique ^e place sur la première et la troisième syllabe. kôukoudoûnou, placer sous. Règle III. — Dans les mots simples de trois syllabes ou plus, à chaque accentuation correspond une syllabe faible, qui est la pénultième. Ex. : silima (pr. : silime). ... Règle IV. — Dans les mots composés, chaque mot simple est soumis aux règles précédentes. ... L'absence de Taccent tonique sert à modifier la signification d'un nom en modifiant la prononciation. En voici quelques exemples, de cas peu fréquent : hû…
readall_conflicts: The standing tension recorded in the catalog bundle remains: the catalog stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 (1 = a stressed syllable) rests on Toque 1904 (dialecte Morouba = moru1251), whose 'accent tonique' is contrastive by presence/absence and hedged as 'qui semblent être très générales', while every modern description of a Central Core Banda lect that the earlier passes reached is three-tone with no accent (Cotel 1907 for Togbo, Arom 2007 for Linda, Olson 2001 for Mono), and Sampson 1985 for Tangbago states 'Stress is noncontrastive on the word level; it is governed by tone and word shape'. The two SIL survey reports on Mbre and Moruba already held by the project (Blühberger 2021, JLSR 2021-013 and 2021-031) say nothing about stress or tone. Tisserant 1930 is the one older primary that might decide whether the initial 'accent' of Toque is stress or tone, and it could not be opened.

audit.recode_to: Downgrade from 'fixed stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 (1 = a stressed syllable) to a tone-language / stress-undescribed (or fixed: initial syllable LOW-CONFIDENCE with caution) entry: caution text 'sole source is a 1904 pre-tonological essay; Banda lects have 3 contrastive level tones (Olson 2001, Althabégoïty 2024); Éboué 1918 equates period 'accent tonique' with pitch; Toqué's accent minimal pairs are probably tonal; only Règle III (final-vowel weakening) is stress-like'. Final choice between 'initial prominence' and 'no word stress' should follow a read of Cloarec-Heiss 1988/1967.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at the stated place in the held Toqué 1904 scanned, and the Morouba = Moruba (Banda-Mbrès) identification is supported by Toqué's own Avertissement. (2) The classification rests entirely on a 1904 colonial administrator's ethnographic essay. Every modern description of a Banda lect we hold or downloaded (Olson 2001 Mono; Althabégoïty 2024 Ngbugu) analyses Banda as a three-level tone language and says nothing about word stress; Éboué 1918, writing on Banda among others, explicitly says the 'accent tonique' of these languages is really high/low pitch. Toqué's list of words distinguished by 'absence of accent' (eau/seins, flèches/arachides, compter/corne) is the signature of lexical tone. So a fixed-stress stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 (1 = a stressed syllable) coded from this source, with no caution flag, is at risk of being a tone misreading; only his final-vowel-weakening rule is independent stress-l
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. confirmed verbatim. lines 2864-2951 (book pp. 63-65, 'ACCENT TONIQUE'): Règles I-IV, 'qu semblent être très générales', 'sUima', 'Taccent tonique ^e place', the 'absence de l'accent tonique' list (hûnga/banga, gongou/gôngou, kôkora/kokora, ngànga/n'ganga, dédé/dédé) and the footnote are all there as quoted; Avertissement lines 279-283 'j'ai dû prendre comme langue principale : le dialecte Morouba.. vallée du Haut-Chari' confirms the Moruba (moru1251, Banda-Mbrès) identification. sources.quote: 'Quant à l'accent tonique, ou plutôt l'intonation, dont l'importance est souvent considérable dans les langues nègres, aussi bien que pour les sons à prononcer sur une note élevée ou sur une note basse, il est impossible de donner ces indications au moyen de signes alphabétiques.' — the contemporaneous usage of 'accent tonique' for Banda etc. denotes pitch, not stress.
